agree.reason: The plain, respectful tone and the guarantee of a job at the same pay or more will win trust, but a long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets little reason to choose it over the severance.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's claim that everyone's job gets better and openly names the harder parts, but 'the wait will get longer' and 'fewer people will start a conversation after 9 minutes' go a little beyond the figures given.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that five branches stay open, but it never turns the severance into concrete terms (ten years means 20 weeks, almost five months of pay) or puts the 44% drop as 'nearly half', and it doesn't project how the trend continues.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is shown as hold times getting longer while calls rise, but it doesn't say what continued falling visits would mean for those two branches if they stayed open.

qualification.reason: The one real condition, the deadline to decide, is left as a placeholder, and the prediction about rising waits comes with no number or date the reader could check.

objections.reason: It names the evening shifts and the change from counter to phone without hiding them, but it gives no answer to 'I don't want to work on the phones', doesn't mention the rumours staff have been hearing for two weeks, and doesn't say how their branch experience carries into the new role.

fit.reason: It's an email from the COO of about 420 words with a clear subject line, though several placeholders still need filling in before it can be sent.
